The test image shows opened soybean pods with seeds visible. Key features:
- Yellow/golden seeds with prominent irregular **black blotchy discoloration/staining** on the seed coats
- One seed mostly yellow with black patches, another heavily black-stained
- Normal-looking mature brown pod walls (hairy, no white mold)

Top candidates based on seed discoloration symptoms: **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (seed mottling/discoloration), **Diaporthe/Phomopsis** (seed shriveling/mold). Let me view reference images.

The **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** reference image (top-right panel) is a near-perfect match — it shows an opened soybean pod with seeds displaying the same distinctive **black irregular blotchy discoloration on yellow/pale seeds**. The test image and this reference image are visually identical in terms of seed appearance, pod morphology, and discoloration pattern.

Diaporthe reference shows stem lesions and pycnidia on stems — not matching.
